newsitem.title: USA: Mid-air collision kills two in Alaska.
newsitem.headline: Mid-air collision kills two in Alaska.

text.p: A collision of two single-engine airplanes over Alaska's Prince William Sound killed two people on Wednesday, the Alaska State Troopers said.
Both airplanes were carrying specialists who were searching for masses of herring in advance of a commercial fishing opening, the troopers said.

One of the planes, not yet identified by type late on Wednesday -- plunged into the sound after the mid-air impact, the troopers said. The other airplane, a Cessna 185, did not crash but made an emergency landing.
The collision occurred at about 1 p.m. (5 p.m. EDT/2100 GMT) over Galena Bay, about 45 miles (70 km) northwest of the fishing town of Cordova, the troopers said.
Dead at the scene was a passenger in the downed aircraft, trooper spokesman Steve Wilhemi said. The passenger, from outside Alaska, was not identified pending family notification.

Rescuers found the pilot, Ronald Gribble, 46, of Homer, Alaska, gravely injured at the site of the downed airplane, Wilhelmi said. He was declared dead shortly afterward at the hospital in Valdez, Wilhelmi said.

Commercial fishermen regularly hire spotters who use airplanes to locate masses of herring. The commercial herring harvest, expected to yield 5,600 tons, is the first in years in Prince William Sound.
